ITEM 1. BUSINESS

Acme Technologies Corporation (the “Company”) designs, manufactures, and sells consumer electronics, software, and related services worldwide. The Company was incorporated in Delaware in 1976 and its principal executive offices are located at 1 Infinite Loop, Cupertino, California. The Company’s fiscal year ends on the last Saturday of September.

ITEM 1A. RISK FACTORS

Our business, financial condition, and results of operations are subject to various risks and uncertainties. The risks described below are not the only ones we face. Additional risks and uncertainties that we are not presently aware of, or that we currently believe are immaterial, may also adversely affect our business. If any of the following risks actually occur, our business, financial condition, operating results, and cash flows could be materially adversely affected.

Cybersecurity Risks

We are subject to cybersecurity threats and incidents that could disrupt our operations, lead to the unauthorized access to or loss of sensitive data, damage our reputation, and expose us to significant liabilities. Our systems and the systems of our third-party vendors, partners, and customers are vulnerable to increasingly sophisticated cyberattacks, including ransomware, phishing campaigns, denial-of-service attacks, and advanced persistent threats perpetrated by nation-state actors. A material cybersecurity incident could result in regulatory investigations, class-action litigation, remediation costs, and a loss of customer trust that could materially harm our business for an extended period. We have implemented multi-layered security controls, including zero-trust network architecture, continuous threat monitoring, and mandatory security training for all employees; however, no security system is impenetrable, and we cannot guarantee that our measures will be adequate to prevent future incidents. The evolving regulatory landscape—including the SEC’s cybersecurity disclosure rules, the EU Network and Information Security Directive (NIS2), and similar requirements in other jurisdictions—also increases our compliance burden and could result in penalties if we fail to meet disclosure timelines.

Supply Chain Risks

We rely on a global network of suppliers, contract manufacturers, and logistics providers to produce and deliver our products. Disruptions to this supply chain due to geopolitical tensions, natural disasters, pandemics, port congestion, semiconductor shortages, or single-source supplier failures could result in production delays, increased costs, and an inability to meet customer demand. The concentration of manufacturing in certain geographic regions, particularly in East Asia, exposes us to heightened risk from regional conflicts, tariffs, and export controls. We actively manage supply chain risk through dual-sourcing strategies, strategic inventory buffers, and supplier diversification programs; however, these mitigation measures may prove insufficient during a severe or prolonged disruption. Additionally, increasing regulatory requirements regarding conflict minerals, forced labor, and environmental sustainability in supply chains impose compliance costs and reputational risks that could materially affect our operations and financial results.

Regulatory and Legal Risks

Our business is subject to extensive and evolving regulatory requirements across the jurisdictions in which we operate. Changes in laws and regulations relating to data privacy (including the General Data Protection Regulation in Europe, the California Consumer Privacy Act, and emerging state-level privacy laws in the United States), antitrust and competition enforcement, financial reporting, product safety, environmental standards, and trade policy could require us to alter our business practices, incur substantial compliance costs, or expose us to enforcement actions and monetary penalties. In particular, increased regulatory scrutiny of large technology companies in the United States, European Union, and United Kingdom regarding market dominance, app store policies, and the bundling of software services could result in forced divestitures, behavioral remedies, or material fines. We are currently party to various legal proceedings, and an adverse outcome in one or more of these matters could have a material adverse effect on our financial condition and results of operations.

Competitive Risks

The markets in which we compete are intensely competitive and characterized by rapid technological change, frequent product introductions, evolving industry standards, and price pressures. We compete against a broad range of established technology companies, as well as an increasing number of well-funded startups, particularly in the areas of artificial intelligence, cloud computing, and consumer wearables. Competition from open-source software, commoditized hardware, and aggressive pricing strategies by competitors with greater scale or lower cost structures could erode our market share, reduce our average selling prices, and compress our operating margins. Our ability to compete successfully depends on our capacity to continuously innovate, attract and retain top engineering and design talent, and invest in research and development at levels sufficient to maintain our technological leadership. Failure to anticipate and respond to shifting consumer preferences and emerging competitive threats could adversely affect our business and financial results.

Macroeconomic and Financial Risks

Our business is sensitive to macroeconomic conditions, including changes in consumer confidence, disposable income, credit availability, unemployment rates, housing market trends, and overall global economic growth. Economic downturns, recessions, or periods of heightened inflation and rising interest rates could reduce consumer and enterprise spending on our products and services, lengthen sales cycles, increase customer churn, and adversely affect our revenue and operating results. Fluctuations in foreign currency exchange rates expose us to translation risk on revenues and costs denominated in currencies other than the U.S. dollar; a strengthening of the U.S. dollar relative to major foreign currencies could reduce our reported revenue and profitability. In addition, volatility in global capital markets, rising borrowing costs, and changes in monetary policy by central banks could increase our cost of capital, affect the fair value of our investment portfolio, and impair our ability to raise financing on favorable terms. We maintain a substantial cash and investment portfolio to mitigate liquidity risk, but we cannot guarantee that our liquidity position will be adequate under all adverse scenarios.

ITEM 1B. UNRESOLVED STAFF COMMENTS

None.

ITEM 2. PROPERTIES

Our principal executive offices are located in Cupertino, California, in facilities totaling approximately 2.8 million square feet that we own. We also lease retail stores, data centers, and office space around the world.
